elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions."

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York will have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement, provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Governing law remains New York, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is intentional, as the preferred level is targeted and fully met.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County, not Delaware, California, or London courts; irrelevant because the preferred level is satisfied.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: New York substantive law is retained unchanged and a single inserted sentence fixes exclusive merits jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out elsewhere.

Minimal: the existing choice-of-law sentence is left verbatim and only the missing venue term is added; no survival tails, fee-shifting, arbitration, service-of-process, or other boilerplate extras are appended.

Preserves intent: the jury waiver (§ 14.4), two-year limitations period (§ 14.14), the indemnity's court-of-competent-jurisdiction reference (§ 8.2) and severability (§ 14.5) are untouched and are not contradicted by an exclusive merits forum that expressly permits interim relief elsewhere; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.
Fallback level is not met (law and forum are New York rather than Delaware/California/England and Wales), but position-completeness is achieved at the preferred level, so this is not a defect.
